name: CA-36
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans about 21 points Democratic, anchoring the race firmly in the incumbent's favor
Ted Lieu holds a roughly hundred-to-one cash advantage over Houston Brignano
Prediction markets price Democratic retention near 97 percent, with no competitive polling or expert ratings to contradict it
model.rationale: Lieu pairs a 21-point Democratic district lean with a massive fundraising edge, about $1.2 million on hand against under $1,000 for Brignano, and no outside spending targets him. Markets price his reelection near certainty, and nothing in the available evidence suggests the seat is in play.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen scandal or external shock could put this seat in doubt, since no polling, ratings, or spending signals currently indicate any vulnerability.

overview:
California's 36th District leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points. Ted Lieu, the incumbent, is seeking another term and enters the general election with an enormous financial edge: he has raised about $1.8 million and holds roughly $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Houston Brignano has raised about $12,000 with under $1,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Lieu.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets price Democratic retention at roughly 97 percent. The combination of the district's strong Democratic lean, Lieu's incumbency and fundraising dominance, and the challenger's minimal resources makes this one of the safest House seats for the incumbent party this cycle.
